output.myth: When Tavo the Gale came down the north cliffs in the thaw, he snatched the washing from every line. Among it was one red mitten, the left one, that belonged to a girl named Mesk who was mending the Spindle's nets beside her grandmother. Aun saw it go up past the Reel and laughed, then felt bad about laughing, which was the usual order for Aun. He cut the string after it to bring it back, and that is why the string is short. Hesk counted the stitches and said nothing. Ennu sewed a new mitten from the sky's own cloth, but it was the wrong colour and would not keep a hand warm. So the Spindle hangs the single mitten on a nail by the hearth. Someone is always looking for the other one. Kael casts his net for it each night and never catches it, and the girl, now grown, says that suits her fine, since she only wanted to be asked.
output.verse:
One cuff on the nail,
someone's hand still reaches out
still wanting its pair.
